case_name: Mahalakshmi Sugar Mills Company Limited and Another v Union of India and Others
petitioner: Mahalakshmi Sugar Mills Company Limited and Another
facts: The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.

What are the factors which are required to be taken into consideration by the Central Government for determining the price of levy sugar in exercise of its power u/s. 3(3C) of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (the Act) is the question involved herein.
The Central Government, in exercise of its power conferred upon it u/s. 3 of the Act, made an order known as the Sugarcane Control Order.

Some of the States in India, however, even prior to coming into force of the said Parliamentary Act, had enacted Legislative Acts, inter alia, providing for to regulation and control of production of sugar.

The Central Government, relying on or on the basis of the recommendations of the said Commission, introduced clause 5A in the said Order as a result whereof additional price came to be paid to the growers of sugarcane (1) over and above the SMP by the sugar producers; (2) equivalent amount from free market sales realization came to be retained by the sugar producer.
Post October 1974, therefore, apart from the levy sugar being based on the SMP only, the same was based on the Actual cane price payable by the sugar producer.

One of the contentions raised in the said writ applications was that 100% mopping up was illegal and the liability of the sugar producers towards the cane growers was to be considered before arriving at the price of levy sugar.
issues: What are the factors which are required to be taken into consideration by the Central Government for determining the price of levy sugar in exercise of its power u/s. 3(3C) of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (the Act)?
The mode of calculation resorted to by the Central Government in determining the price of levy sugar, particularly, the effect of clause 5A of the Sugarcane Control Order.
Whether the liability of the sugar producers towards the cane growers was to be considered before arriving at the price of levy sugar.
petitioner_arguments: The Central Government continued with the exercise of determination of the price of levy sugar on the basis of 100% mopping up and had not been considering the said changed scenario.

respondent_arguments: The Central Government, relying on or on the basis of the recommendations of the said Commission, introduced clause 5A in the said Order as a result whereof additional price came to be paid to the growers of sugarcane (1) over and above the SMP by the sugar producers; (2) equivalent amount from free market sales realization came to be retained by the sugar producer.
The Central Government continued with the exercise of determination of the price of levy sugar on the basis of 100% mopping up and had not been considering the said changed scenario.
court_reasoning: In paragraph 2.15 the details of the scheme were given as follows:
It is true that Clause 5-A deals with additional price payable to the sugar-cane grower.

The statutory minimum price for sugarcane related to a basic recovery of 8.6 per cent with a premium for every 0.1 per cent increase in recovery on proportionality basis will be fixed by the Government of India.
holding: The Central Government, relying on or on the basis of the recommendations of the said Commission, introduced clause 5A in the said Order as a result whereof additional price came to be paid to the growers of sugarcane (1) over and above the SMP by the sugar producers; (2) equivalent amount from free market sales realization came to be retained by the sugar producer.
The liability of the sugar producers towards the cane growers was to be considered before arriving at the price of levy sugar.
